parsed.title: A Number of Critical Scholars Often Date These Biblical Creeds to the 30s AD - Gary Habermas
parsed.summary: This is a historical-apologetics chapter in which Gary Habermas argues that early Christian creeds (1 Corinthians 15:3ff, Romans 10:9, Romans 1:3-4) predate 50 AD and likely go back to the 30s AD, citing even critical scholars (the Jesus Seminar, Bart Ehrman) who concede the creed existed before Paul's conversion. The material is evidential/historical rather than systematic-theological: it supplies empirical support for the early, non-mythologized transmission of the deity-death-resurrection proclamation, which touches the canon's evidence layer (EV15.1 biblical validation) and the information-conservation/transmission concerns (BC7) but does not assert or engage the formal axiom nodes about coherence, chi, phi, grace operators, or the master equation.

axiom_nodes.name: EV15.1 — Biblical Prophecy Validation
axiom_nodes.evidence_quote: So I think that's the Jesus Seminar I'm citing.
axiom_nodes.notes: The chapter supplies historical-evidence reasoning for the reliability/early dating of biblical creedal material, functioning as evidence-layer support for scriptural validation, though it argues from creeds rather than prophecy.

axiom_nodes.name: BC7 — Information Conservation
axiom_nodes.evidence_quote: What keeps the creeds from being expanded until they become myth and they're not really the words of the eyewitnesses.
axiom_nodes.notes: Habermas's concern that the creedal content was preserved without mythological corruption is conceptually adjacent to information conservation across transmission, but he makes a historiographical argument, not an information-theoretic claim.

axiom_nodes.name: P9.3 — Information Preserved Under Grace
axiom_nodes.notes: The preservation of the early gospel content (deity, death, resurrection) is thematically near information preservation, but the source does not frame it in terms of grace or the formal axiom.
